profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite cluster spans Los Angeles, San Jose, Santa Clara, and Santa Clara County, California, the company founding home turf. Wikipedia coverage states CoreSite was established in 2001 as CRG West, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. In May 2007 the company acquired Santa Clara land for a planned 50 megawatt data center as part of a wider expansion that also added Boston and Chicago properties. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. As of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with Los Angeles and San Francisco/San Jose/Santa Clara both listed among its key markets. American Tower completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
The San Jose Colocation Center is a 320,000 square foot facility in downtown San Jose operated by CoreSite, now under American Tower. Its published capacity is not stated, which places it outside the 11 California facilities that have disclosed megawatts. Among mapped data centers in the state, this campus does not rank in the top 11 by published power, though 103 facilities exist statewide with only 365 MW total capacity disclosed across all of them.

The facility holds certifications for SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 audit compliance, ISO 27001 information security, NIST 800-53 security controls, PCI DSS payment card processing, and HIPAA healthcare data handling. These certifications establish baseline security and compliance posture but do not reveal capacity or intended tenant profile.

Without published megawatt figures, the practical significance of this campus for AI scaling cannot be assessed from operator disclosures. The absence of capacity data, combined with its downtown San Jose location in a market where CoreSite operates multiple properties, suggests this may be a smaller or specialized facility within a regional cluster, but this remains inference rather than published fact.
